translations.idiomatic: Qiqiu and Xu Rong were present. Shan raised his cup and said, "Snow falling thick—that's Bai Qi (White Rise)."

sentences.zh: 齊丘曰：「著屐過街，必須雍齒。」

translations.literal: Qiqiu said, "Wearing clogs to cross the street—that must be Yong Chi."
translations.idiomatic: Qiqiu answered, "Clogs in the street—that's Yong Chi (Yong Teeth)."

sentences.zh: 融意欲挫掞等，遽曰：「明朝日出，爭奈蕭何。」

translations.literal: Rong wished to humble Shan and the others and blurted, "When the sun comes out tomorrow, what can be done about Xiao He?"
translations.idiomatic: Rong, trying to cut them down, shot back, "When the sun rises tomorrow—what about Xiao He?" implying their day would end."

sentences.zh: 掞大怒，是夜收融投於江，自是與謀者惟齊丘而已。

translations.literal: Shan was greatly enraged; that night he seized Rong and cast him into the river, and from then on his only fellow plotter was Qiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: Shan was furious. That night he had Rong thrown into the river, and afterward Qiqiu alone shared his plots.

sentences.zh: 宋齊丘，豫章人，父嘗在鐘傳幕下。

translations.literal: Song Qiqiu was a man of Yuzhang; his father had once served on Zhong Chuan's staff.
translations.idiomatic: Song Qiqiu was from Yuzhang. His father had once served under Zhong Chuan.

sentences.zh: 齊丘素落魄，父卒，家計蕩盡，已在窮悴，朝夕不能度。

translations.literal: Qiqiu had always been down on his luck; when his father died the family fortune was utterly spent, and he was already in destitution, unable to get through from morning to night.
translations.idiomatic: Qiqiu had always been down on his luck. After his father died the family fortune vanished and he was destitute, barely surviving day to day.

sentences.zh: 時姚洞天為淮南騎將，素好士，齊丘欲謁之，且囊空無備紙筆之費，計無所出，但於逆旅社門而坐，如此殆數日。

translations.literal: At that time Yao Dongtian was a Huainan cavalry officer and by nature loved scholars; Qiqiu wished to call on him, yet his purse was empty and he had no money to prepare paper and brush; finding no way out, he only sat at the gate of the inn's lodge, thus for nearly several days.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Dongtian, a Huainan cavalry officer who loved scholars, was someone Qiqiu wanted to meet, but he had no money even for paper and ink. For days he simply sat at the inn gate, unable to think of a way forward.

sentences.zh: 鄰房有散樂女尚幼，問齊丘曰：「秀才何以數日不出？」

translations.literal: In the neighboring room was a young female performer of itinerant music still a child; she asked Qiqiu, "Scholar, why have you not gone out for several days?"
translations.idiomatic: A young traveling entertainer in the next room asked him, "Scholar, why haven't you left your room for days?"

sentences.zh: 齊丘以實告，女嘆曰：「此甚小事，秀才何吝一言相示耶！」

translations.literal: Qiqiu told her the truth; the girl sighed and said, "This is a very small matter—Scholar, why be stingy about speaking a word to show it!"
translations.idiomatic: He told her the truth. She sighed and said, "That's nothing—you only had to ask!"

sentences.zh: 乃惠以數緡。

translations.literal: She then gave him several strings of cash as a kindness.
translations.idiomatic: She gave him a few strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 齊丘用市紙筆，為詩詠以投洞天，其略曰：「某學武無成，攻文失誌，歲華蹭蹬，身事蹉跎。

translations.literal: Qiqiu used them to buy paper and brush, composed a poem to present to Dongtian, the gist of which ran, "I studied arms without success, pursued letters and lost my aim; the years slip stumbling by, and my life's affairs drag in delay.
translations.idiomatic: Qiqiu bought paper and brush and sent Dongtian a poem that began, "I studied arms without success and letters without reward; the years slip by and my life goes nowhere.

sentences.zh: 胸中之萬仞青山，壓低氣宇；

translations.literal: The ten-thousand-ren green mountains in my breast press down my spirit;
translations.idiomatic: Ten-thousand-ren green mountains in my breast weigh down my spirit;

sentences.zh: 頭上之一輪紅日，燒盡風雲。

translations.literal: the one round red sun upon my head burns away wind and clouds;
translations.idiomatic: one red sun above my head burns away every storm;

sentences.zh: 加以天步淩遲，皇綱廢絕，四海淵黑，中原血紅。

translations.literal: moreover Heaven's step falters, the royal net is abolished, the four seas are abyss-deep black, the Central Plains blood-red;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven itself staggers, imperial order lies in ruins, the four seas sink into darkness, the heartland runs red with blood;

sentences.zh: 挹飛蒼走黃之辯，有出鬼沒神之機。」

translations.literal: I draw on the disputation of 'flying azure' and 'running yellow,' and possess stratagems that emerge like ghosts and vanish like spirits."
translations.idiomatic: I wield a huntsman's eloquence and a wit that appears and vanishes like spirits."

sentences.zh: 洞天怒其言大，不即接見。

translations.literal: Dongtian was angered that his words were too grand and did not immediately receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Dongtian took offense at such grand language and refused to see him at once.

sentences.zh: 齊丘窘急，乃更其啟，翌日復至，其略曰：「有生不如無生，為人不若為鬼。」

translations.literal: Qiqiu, in distress, rewrote his letter and returned the next day; the gist ran, "To live is not as good as not to live; to be human is not as good as being a ghost."
translations.idiomatic: Desperate, Qiqiu rewrote his letter and came back the next day with a plea that ran, "Better never to have lived than to live; better to be a ghost than a man."

sentences.zh: 又云：「其為誠懇萬端，只為饑寒兩字。」

translations.literal: He also wrote, "My earnestness has ten thousand forms, only for the two words hunger and cold."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "My earnestness knows no end--all for two words: hunger and cold."

sentences.zh: 洞天始憫之，漸加以拯救。

translations.literal: Dongtian then pitied him and gradually came to his rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Dongtian took pity on him and little by little pulled him back from ruin.

sentences.zh: 徐溫聞其名，召至門下。

translations.literal: Xu Wen heard his name and summoned him to his staff.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Wen heard of him and took him into his household.

sentences.zh: 及掞之有江南也，齊丘以佐命功，遂至將相，乃上表以散樂女為妻，以報宿惠，許之。

translations.literal: When Shan came to possess Jiangnan, Qiqiu for his merit in founding the regime rose to general and chancellor; he then submitted a memorial to take the itinerant entertainer girl as wife to repay an old kindness, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Bian held Jiangnan, Qiqiu rose to general and chancellor for helping found the regime. He memorialized the throne to marry the traveling entertainer who had once helped him, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 韓熙載仕江南，官至諸行侍郎。

translations.literal: Han Xizai served in Jiangnan and reached the office of Vice Director of Miscellaneous Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Han Xizai served in Jiangnan and rose to Vice Director of Miscellaneous Affairs.

sentences.zh: 晚年不羈，女仆百人，每延請賓客，而先令女仆與之相見，或調戲，或毆擊，或加以爭奪靴笏，無不曲盡，然後熙載始緩步而出，習以為常。

translations.literal: In his later years he was unrestrained and kept a hundred female servants; whenever he entertained guests he first had the servants appear before them--some flirting, some striking blows, some scrambling for boots and tally--every display to the full; only then would Xizai saunter out, and it became habitual.
translations.idiomatic: In old age he lived without restraint, keeping a hundred maidservants. Whenever he entertained guests he had the maids appear first--flirting, brawling, snatching boots and tally sticks--every spectacle played out in full before Xizai strolled out at last. It became routine.

sentences.zh: 復有醫人及燒煉僧數輩，每來無不升堂入室，與女仆等雜處，偽主知之，雖怒，以其大臣，不欲直指其過，因命待詔畫為圖以賜之，使其自愧，而熙載視之安然。）〉

translations.literal: There were also several physicians and alchemist monks who, whenever they came, invariably entered hall and chamber and mixed with the female servants and the like. The usurper sovereign learned of it; though angry, because Xizai was a great minister he did not wish to point directly at the fault, and so ordered a court artist to paint a picture and bestow it, hoping to shame him--yet Xizai viewed it calmly.〉
translations.idiomatic: Physicians and alchemist monks also came and went freely through his halls, mingling with the maids. The court knew and was furious, but because Xizai was a senior minister it did not rebuke him openly. Instead it had a court painter record the scene and sent him the picture to shame him. Xizai looked at it without a flicker of embarrassment.〉

sentences.zh: 王審知，字信通，光州固始人。

translations.literal: Wang Shenzhi, style name Xintong, was a man of Gushi in Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shenzhi, courtesy name Xintong, was a native of Gushi in Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父恁，世為農民。

translations.literal: His father Ren's family had been farmers for generations.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ren came from a farming family.

sentences.zh: 唐廣明中，黃巢犯闕，江、淮盜賊蜂起。

translations.literal: In the Guangming era of Tang, Huang Chao attacked the capital, and bandits rose everywhere through the Jiang and Huai regions.
translations.idiomatic: During Tang Guangming, Huang Chao stormed the capital and bandits swarmed across the Jiang-Huai region.

sentences.zh: 有賊帥王緒者，自稱將軍，陷固始縣，審知兄潮時為縣佐，緒署為軍正。

translations.literal: There was a bandit chief Wang Xu who styled himself general, captured Gushi county, and at that time Shenzhi's elder brother Chao was a county aide; Xu appointed him army rectifier.
translations.idiomatic: A bandit leader named Wang Xu styled himself general, seized Gushi county, and appointed Shenzhi's elder brother Chao, then a county aide, as army rectifier.

sentences.zh: 蔡賊秦宗權以緒為光州刺史，尋遣兵攻之，緒率眾渡江，所在剽掠，自南康轉至閩中，入臨汀，自稱刺史。

translations.literal: The Cai bandit Qin Zongquan made Xu prefect of Guangzhou, then soon sent troops to attack him; Xu led his followers across the Yangtze, plundering wherever he went, turned from Nankang into Min territory, entered Lin Ting, and styled himself prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan of Cai made Xu prefect of Guangzhou, then attacked him. Xu led his men across the Yangtze, looting as he went from Nankang into Fujian and on to Lin Ting, where he styled himself prefect.

sentences.zh: 緒多疑忌，部將有出己之右者皆誅之。

translations.literal: Xu was suspicious and jealous; subordinate officers who surpassed him were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was suspicious and jealous and killed any subordinate who outshone him.

sentences.zh: 潮與豪首數輩共殺緒，其眾求帥，乃刑牲歃血為盟，植劍於前，祝曰：「拜此劍動者為將軍。」

translations.literal: Chao with several bold leaders jointly killed Xu; the troops sought a commander, so they slaughtered a beast and swore a blood oath, planted a sword before them, and prayed, "Whoever bowing makes this sword move shall be general."
translations.idiomatic: Chao and several bold leaders killed Xu. The army wanted a new commander, so they sacrificed an animal, swore a blood oath, planted a sword before them, and prayed, "Whoever makes this sword move when he bows shall be general."

sentences.zh: 至潮拜，劍躍於地，眾以為神異，即奉潮為帥。

translations.literal: When Chao bowed, the sword leaped to the ground; all thought it miraculous and immediately hailed Chao as commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao bowed, the sword sprang from the ground. The men took it as a sign and made Chao their leader.

sentences.zh: 時泉州刺史廖彥若為政貪暴，軍民若之，聞潮為理整肅，耆老乃奉牛酒，遮道請留。

translations.literal: At that time Quanzhou prefect Liao Yanruo governed with greed and cruelty; soldiers and civilians resented him. Hearing that Chao's rule was orderly and strict, elders brought oxen and wine, blocked the road, and asked him to stay.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhou prefect Liao Yanruo ruled with greed and cruelty, and the people hated him. When they heard that Chao governed with discipline, elders met him on the road with oxen and wine and begged him to stay.

sentences.zh: 潮因引兵圍彥若，歲餘克之，又平狼山賊帥薛蘊，兵鋒日盛。

translations.literal: Chao thereupon led troops to besiege Yanruo; after more than a year he captured him, also pacified Lang Mountain bandit chief Xue Yun, and his military edge grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Chao besieged Yanruo and took the city after more than a year. He also crushed Lang Mountain bandit chief Xue Yun, and his army grew stronger by the day.

sentences.zh: 唐光啟二年，福建觀察使陳巖表潮為泉州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tang Guangqi, Fujian observation commissioner Chen Yan memorialized Chao as Quanzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang Guangqi 2, Fujian observation commissioner Chen Yan recommended Chao for Quanzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 大順中，巖卒，子婿範暉自稱留後，潮遣審知將兵攻之，逾年，城中食盡，乃斬暉而降，由是盡有閩、嶺五州之地。

translations.literal: During Dazhong, Chen Yan died and his son-in-law Fan Hui styled himself acting governor; Chao sent Shenzhi to lead troops against him. After more than a year the city's provisions were exhausted; they beheaded Hui and surrendered, and thereby fully possessed the five prefectures of Min and the mountain region.
translations.idiomatic: During Dazhong, Chen Yan died and his son-in-law Fan Hui declared himself acting governor. Chao sent Shenzhi to besiege him. After more than a year the city ran out of food, Hui was killed, and the garrison surrendered. Chao then held all five prefectures of Fujian and the surrounding hills.

sentences.zh: 潮即表其事，昭宗因建威武軍於福州，以潮為節度、福建管內觀察使，審知為副。

translations.literal: Chao immediately memorialized the matter; Zhaozong thereupon established the Weiwu Army at Fuzhou, made Chao military commissioner and Fujian circuit observation commissioner, and Shenzhi deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Chao reported this to court. Emperor Zhaozong established the Weiwu Army at Fuzhou, made Chao its military commissioner and Fujian observation commissioner, and appointed Shenzhi his deputy.

sentences.zh: 審知為觀察副使，有過，潮猶加捶撻，審知無怨色。

translations.literal: Shenzhi served as observation vice commissioner; when he had faults Chao still beat him, yet Shenzhi showed no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: As observation vice commissioner, Shenzhi was beaten by Chao even for minor faults, yet he never showed resentment.

sentences.zh: 潮寢疾，舍其子延興、延虹、延豐、延休，命審知知軍府事。

translations.literal: Chao fell ill in bed, set aside his sons Yanxing, Yanhong, Yanfeng, and Yanxiu, and ordered Shenzhi to manage military headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Chao fell ill he passed over his sons Yanxing, Yanhong, Yanfeng, and Yanxiu and put Shenzhi in charge of the army headquarters.

sentences.zh: 十二月丁未，潮薨，審知以讓其兄審邽，審邽以審知有功，辭不受。

translations.literal: On dingwei day of the twelfth month Chao died; Shenzhi yielded the post to his elder brother Shengui, but Shengui, because Shenzhi had merit, declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei day of the twelfth month Chao died. Shenzhi offered command to his elder brother Shengui, but Shengui refused, saying Shenzhi had earned it.

sentences.zh: 審知自稱福建留後，表於朝廷。

translations.literal: Shenzhi styled himself Fujian acting governor and memorialized the court.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzhi declared himself Fujian acting governor and reported it to court.

sentences.zh: 唐末，為威武軍節度、福建觀察使，累遷檢校太保，封瑯邪郡王。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang he served as Weiwu Army military commissioner and Fujian observation commissioner, was repeatedly promoted to honorary Grand Guardian, and was enfeoffed Prince of Langya Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of Tang he was Weiwu Army military commissioner and Fujian observation commissioner, rose to honorary Grand Guardian, and was enfeoffed Prince of Langya.

sentences.zh: 梁朝開國，累加中書令，封閩王。

translations.literal: When the Liang dynasty was founded he was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed Prince of Min.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang was founded he was made Director of the Secretariat and enfeoffed Prince of Min.

sentences.zh: 〈（《王審知德政碑》云：潮付公以戎旅，仍具表奏，尋加刑部尚書、威武軍留後，俄授金紫光祿大夫、右僕射、本軍節度使，又改光祿大夫、檢校司空，轉特進、檢校司徒，又轉檢校太保、瑯邪郡王，食邑四千戶，食實封一百戶。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Wang Shenzhi Virtue-Governance Stele》 says: Chao entrusted the Duke with the army and jointly submitted a memorial; soon he was added Minister of Justice and Weiwu Army acting governor; shortly he was invested Grand Master of Golden Brightness and Purple Splendor, Right Vice Director, and military commissioner of this army; again changed to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and honorary Minister of Works; transferred to Superlative Pillar and honorary Minister of Education; again transferred to honorary Grand Guardian and Prince of Langya Commandery, with a fief of four thousand households and an actual fief of one hundred households.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Wang Shenzhi Virtue-Governance Stele》 records that Chao put Shenzhi in command of the army and memorialized court together with him; soon Shenzhi was made Minister of Justice and Weiwu Army acting governor, then Grand Master of Golden Brightness and Purple Splendor, Right Vice Director, and military commissioner of the army; later Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and honorary Minister of Works; then Superlative Pillar and honorary Minister of Education; then honorary Grand Guardian and Prince of Langya, with a nominal fief of four thousand households and an actual fief of one hundred.)〉

sentences.zh: 是時，楊氏據江、淮，故閩中與中國隔越，審知每歲朝貢，泛海至登萊抵岸，往復頗有風水之患，漂沒者十四五。

translations.literal: At this time the Yang clan held the Jiang and Huai regions, so Min was cut off from China; Shenzhi each year sent tribute, crossing the sea to Deng and Lai to reach shore; going back and forth there were many wind-and-water hazards, and fourteen or fifteen out of every hundred were lost at sea.
translations.idiomatic: The Yang clan then held the Jiang-Huai region, isolating Fujian from the central court. Shenzhi sent tribute every year by sea to Deng and Lai. The voyage was perilous; fourteen or fifteen ships in every hundred were lost.

sentences.zh: 後唐莊宗即位，遣使奉貢，制加功臣，進爵邑。

translations.literal: When Later Tang Zhuangzong took the throne, Shenzhi sent envoys with tribute; an edict added merit titles and advanced his fief.
translations.idiomatic: When Later Tang Zhuangzong came to the throne, Shenzhi sent tribute envoys and received an edict adding merit titles and enlarging his fief.

sentences.zh: 審知起自隴畝，以至富貴。

translations.literal: Shenzhi rose from the fields to reach wealth and honor.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzhi rose from the fields to great wealth and rank.

sentences.zh: 每以節儉自處，選任良吏，省刑惜費，輕徭薄斂，與民休息。

translations.literal: He always practiced frugality toward himself, selected good officials, reduced punishments and economized expenses, lightened corvee and kept levies thin, and rested with the people.
translations.idiomatic: He lived frugally, appointed capable officials, eased punishments and spending, lightened labor and taxes, and let the people recover.

sentences.zh: 三十年間，一境晏然。

translations.literal: Within thirty years the whole territory was tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: For thirty years his domain remained at peace.

sentences.zh: 同光元年，審知卒，子延翰嗣，為弟延鈞所殺。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongguang, Shenzhi died; his son Yanhan succeeded, and was killed by his younger brother Yanjun.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongguang 1 Shenzhi died. His son Yanhan succeeded him but was killed by his younger brother Yanjun.

sentences.zh: 延鈞，審知次子。

translations.literal: Yanjun was Shenzhi's second son.
translations.idiomatic: Yanjun was Shenzhi's second son.

sentences.zh: 後唐長興三年，上言吳越國王錢镠薨，乞封為吳越王，不報。

translations.literal: In the third year of Later Tang Changxing he submitted a memorial saying that Wuyue king Qian Liu had died and requesting to be enfeoffed Prince of Wuyue; there was no response.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Tang Changxing 3 he memorialized that Wuyue king Qian Liu had died and asked to be made Prince of Wuyue. Court did not reply.

sentences.zh: 未幾，自稱帝，國號大閩，改元龍啟，然猶稱藩於朝廷。

translations.literal: Before long he styled himself emperor, set the state name as Great Min, changed the era to Longqi, yet still styled himself a vassal of the court.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he declared himself emperor, named his state Great Min, and changed the era to Longqi, while still presenting himself as a vassal of the central court.

sentences.zh: 清泰元年，遇弒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qingtai he met assassination.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingtai 1 he was assassinated.

sentences.zh: 子昶嗣。

translations.literal: His son Chang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 昶，嗣偽位，朝廷因授昶福建節度使。

translations.literal: Chang succeeded to the false throne, and the court thereupon invested Chang as Fujian military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Chang took the throne, and the court invested him as Fujian military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 晉天福三年，遣使貢奉至闕，止稱閩王。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jin Tianfu he sent envoys with tribute to the palace, styling himself only Prince of Min.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin Tianfu 3 he sent tribute envoys to court and styled himself only Prince of Min.

sentences.zh: 其子繼恭稱節度使，晉祖乃下制封昶為閩王。

translations.literal: His son Jigong styled himself military commissioner; the Jin founder then issued an edict enfeoffing Chang as Prince of Min.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jigong styled himself military commissioner, so the Jin founder issued an edict making Chang Prince of Min.

sentences.zh: 改元通大，後遇弒，審知少子延羲嗣。

translations.literal: He changed the era to Tongda; later he met assassination, and Shenzhi's youngest son Yanxi succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He changed the era to Tongda, was later assassinated, and Shenzhi's youngest son Yanxi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 延羲，嗣偽位，改元永隆，在位六年遇弒。

translations.literal: Yanxi succeeded to the false throne, changed the era to Yonglong, and in the sixth year of his reign met assassination.
translations.idiomatic: Yanxi took the throne, changed the era to Yonglong, and was assassinated in his sixth year.

sentences.zh: 兄延政，自稱帝於福州，晉開運三年，為李景所滅。

translations.literal: His elder brother Yanzheng styled himself emperor at Fuzhou; in the third year of Jin Kaiyun he was destroyed by Li Jing.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Yanzheng declared himself emperor at Fuzhou. In Jin Kaiyun 3 Li Jing destroyed him.

sentences.zh: 〈（《五代史補》：王潮之來福建也，值連帥陳巖卒，子婿範暉自稱留後，潮攻拔之，盡有其地，遂為福建觀察使。

translations.literal: (The Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties says: When Wang Chao came to Fujian, it happened that the regional commander Chen Yan died; his son-in-law Fan Hui styled himself acting governor. Chao attacked and seized it, fully possessed the territory, and thus became Fujian observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: (The Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties records that when Wang Chao entered Fujian, regional commander Chen Yan had just died and his son-in-law Fan Hui had declared himself acting governor. Chao captured the territory, took possession of the whole province, and became Fujian observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 至其弟審知立，雖天下多事，猶能修其職貢，朝廷嘉之，封閩王。

translations.literal: When his younger brother Shenzhi came to power, although the empire was beset by many troubles, he was still able to maintain tribute duties; the court commended this and enfeoffed him as King of Min.
translations.idiomatic: When his brother Shenzhi took over, he kept up regular tribute despite the chaos throughout the realm, and the court rewarded him with the title King of Min.

sentences.zh: 審知卒，子延鈞嗣，無識，輒改審知制度，僭稱大閩，改元龍啟，其後為子昶殺。

translations.literal: When Shenzhi died, his son Yanjun succeeded; lacking discernment, he rashly changed Shenzhi's institutions, arrogated the title Great Min, changed the era name to Longqi, and afterward was killed by his son Chang.
translations.idiomatic: After Shenzhi's death his son Yanjun succeeded him. Shortsighted and rash, Yanjun overturned his father's institutions, proclaimed the state Great Min, and adopted the era name Longqi; later his son Chang killed him.

sentences.zh: 昶多行不道，閩人殺之。

translations.literal: Chang committed many wicked acts; the people of Min killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Chang ruled wickedly, and the people of Min put him to death.

sentences.zh: 立從父延羲，改元永隆，延羲不恤政事，國亂，為其將連重遇所殺，王氏之族遂滅。

translations.literal: They enthroned his paternal uncle Yanxi, who changed the era name to Yonglong; Yanxi paid no heed to affairs of government, the state fell into disorder, and he was killed by his general Lian Chongyu — and thus the Wang clan was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: They enthroned his uncle Yanxi, who adopted the era name Yonglong. Yanxi neglected government, the realm fell into turmoil, and his general Lian Chongyu killed him — ending the Wang line.

sentences.zh: 先是，梁朝有王霸者，即王氏之遠祖，為道士，居於福州之怡山時，愛二皂莢樹，因其下築壇，為朝禮之所，其後丹成沖虛而去，霸嘗云：「吾之子孫，當有王於此方者。」

translations.literal: Earlier, during the Liang dynasty there was one Wang Ba, a distant ancestor of the Wang clan; he was a Daoist priest, and while living at Yishan in Fuzhou he loved two soap-pod trees, and beneath them built an altar as a place for ritual worship. Later, when his elixir was perfected he rose into immortality and departed. Ba once said: "My descendants shall have one who becomes king in this region."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Liang dynasty, a distant Wang forebear named Wang Ba had been a Daoist priest on Mount Yi in Fuzhou. He cherished two honeylocust trees and built an altar beneath them for ritual devotions. When his elixir-work was complete he ascended as an immortal and vanished. Ba once declared, "A descendant of mine will reign as king in this place."

sentences.zh: 乃自為讖，藏之於地。

translations.literal: He thereupon composed a prophecy himself and buried it in the ground.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote his own prophecy and buried it in the earth.

sentences.zh: 唐光啟中，爛柯道士徐景元，因於壇東北隅取土，獲其詩，曰：「樹枯不用伐，壇壞不須結。

translations.literal: In the Guangqi reign of Tang, the Lankao Daoist Xu Jingyuan, while taking earth from the northeast corner of the altar, obtained his poem, which read: "When the trees wither there is no need to fell them; when the altar collapses there is no need to repair it.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tang Guangqi era, the Lankao Daoist Xu Jingyuan took soil from the altar's northeast corner and recovered the verse. It read: "Let the trees die — no need to cut them; let the altar crumble — no need to mend it.

sentences.zh: 不滿一千年，自有系孫列。」

translations.literal: Before a thousand years have passed, descendants of the lineage will appear in succession."
translations.idiomatic: In less than a thousand years, a line of heirs will arise in turn."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「後來是三王，潮水蕩禍殃。

translations.literal: It also said: "Later there will be three kings; the tide will wash away calamity and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Another line ran: "Three kings will follow; the tidal wave will scour away doom and ruin.

sentences.zh: 巖逢二乍間，未免有銷亡。

translations.literal: When Yan encounters the interval of two moments, there will unavoidably be destruction and extinction.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan meets the span between two 'moments,' some destruction cannot be avoided.

sentences.zh: 子孫依吾道，代代封閩疆。」

translations.literal: Descendants who follow my Way shall generation after generation be enfeoffed over the borders of Min."
translations.idiomatic: Heirs who keep to my path will hold Min's domain, generation after generation."

sentences.zh: 議者以為：潮蕩禍殃，謂王潮除其禍患以開基業也；

translations.literal: Commentators held: "The tide washing away calamity and disaster" refers to Wang Chao removing disasters and troubles to establish the foundation;
translations.idiomatic: Commentators interpreted "the tide scouring doom and ruin" as Wang Chao clearing away threats to lay his foundations;

sentences.zh: 巖逢二乍間，謂陳巖逢王潮未幾而亡，土地為其所有也；

translations.literal: "When Yan encounters the interval of two moments" refers to Chen Yan encountering Wang Chao and not long afterward dying, with the land becoming his possession;
translations.idiomatic: "Yan meeting the span between two 'moments'" meant Chen Yan encountering Wang Chao and dying soon after, his territory passing into Wang hands;

sentences.zh: 代代封閩疆，謂潮與審知也，代代蓋兩世之稱，明封崇不過潮與審知兩世耳。

translations.literal: "Generation after generation enfeoffed over the borders of Min" refers to Chao and Shenzhi — "generation after generation" is likely a term for two generations, making clear that honors and enfeoffments extended no further than Chao and Shenzhi for two generations.
translations.idiomatic: "Holding Min from generation to generation" referred to Chao and Shenzhi alone — "generation after generation" being a way of counting two reigns, showing that royal favor reached only those two men.

sentences.zh: 初，王潮嘗假道於洪州，時鐘傳為洪州節度使，以王潮若得福建，境土相接，必為己患，陰欲誅之。

translations.literal: Initially, Wang Chao once passed through Hongzhou by borrowed route; at that time Zhong Chuan was military governor of Hongzhou. He thought that if Wang Chao obtained Fujian and their territories adjoined, Chao would certainly become a menace to him, and secretly wished to execute him.
translations.idiomatic: Once, when Wang Chao was passing through Hongzhou, Zhong Chuan was its military governor. Chuan feared that if Chao secured Fujian their lands would border each other and Chao would become a permanent threat, and he secretly planned to kill him.

sentences.zh: 有僧上藍者，通於術數，動皆先知，大為鐘所重。

translations.literal: There was a monk named Shanglan who was skilled in numerology and divination; his every movement was foreknown in advance, and Zhong greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: A monk named Shanglan, versed in divination and prophecy, seemed to know events before they happened and was held in great esteem by Zhong Chuan.

sentences.zh: 因入謁，察傳詞氣，驚曰：「令公何故起惡意，是欲殺王潮否？」

translations.literal: Entering to pay his respects, he observed Chuan's tone and was startled, saying: "Why does the Lord raise evil intent — do you mean to kill Wang Chao?"
translations.idiomatic: On a visit to pay respects, Shanglan detected malice in Chuan's manner and cried out, "Why this dark intent, my lord? Do you mean to kill Wang Chao?"

sentences.zh: 傳不敢隱，盡以告之。

translations.literal: Chuan dared not conceal it and told him everything.
translations.idiomatic: Chuan did not dare hide the truth and confessed the whole plan.

sentences.zh: 上藍曰：「老僧觀王潮與福建有緣，必變，彼時作一好世界。

translations.literal: Shanglan said: "This old monk sees that Wang Chao shares a karmic bond with Fujian; he will certainly transform that place, and at that time make a fine world there.
translations.idiomatic: Shanglan said, "I see that Wang Chao is bound to Fujian by fate. He will change that land and one day make a flourishing realm of it.

sentences.zh: 令公宜加禮厚待，若必殺之，令公之福去矣。」

translations.literal: The Lord ought to treat him with courtesy and generous hospitality; if you insist on killing him, the Lord's blessings will depart."
translations.idiomatic: Treat him with honor and generous support. If you kill him, your own good fortune will vanish."

sentences.zh: 於是傳加以援送。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chuan gave him additional aid and escort.
translations.idiomatic: Chuan thereupon furnished Chao with extra support and safe passage.

sentences.zh: 及審知之嗣位也，楊行密方盛，常有吞東南之志氣。

translations.literal: When Shenzhi succeeded to the throne, Yang Xingmi was at the height of his power and constantly harbored ambition to swallow the southeast.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Shenzhi inherited rule, Yang Xingmi was at the height of his power and often spoke of conquering the southeast.

sentences.zh: 審知居常憂之，因其先人嘗為上藍所知，乃使人賫金帛往遺之，號曰「送供」，且問國之休咎。

translations.literal: Shenzhi was ordinarily worried about this; because his predecessor had once been known to Shanglan, he sent men bearing gold and silk as gifts to Shanglan, calling it "offering supplies," and also inquired about the fortunes of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Shenzhi lived in constant anxiety over this threat. Remembering that Shanglan had once aided his brother, he sent gold and silk as a "sustaining offering" and asked what lay in store for the realm.

sentences.zh: 使回，上藍以十字為報，其詞曰：「不怕羊入屋，只怕錢入腹。」

translations.literal: When the envoy returned, Shanglan replied in ten characters; the words were: "Do not fear the sheep entering the house; only fear money entering the belly."
translations.idiomatic: When the messenger returned, Shanglan answered in ten characters: "Fear not the sheep entering the house — fear only money entering the belly."

sentences.zh: 審知得之嘆曰：「羊者楊也，腹者福也，得非福州之患，不在楊行密而在錢氏乎？

translations.literal: When Shenzhi received this he sighed and said: "Sheep refers to Yang; belly refers to Fu — could it be that Fuzhou's trouble lies not with Yang Xingmi but with the Qian clan?
translations.idiomatic: Reading the answer, Shenzhi sighed and said, "Sheep stands for Yang, and belly for Fu — does this mean Fuzhou's danger lies not with Yang Xingmi but with the house of Qian?

sentences.zh: 今內外將吏無姓錢者，必為子孫後世之憂矣。」

translations.literal: Now there are no officers within or without surnamed Qian — this must be a concern for later generations of descendants.
translations.idiomatic: We have no commanders or officials surnamed Qian today — yet this must be a warning for generations yet to come."

sentences.zh: 至延羲為連重遇所殺，諸將爭立，江南乘其時命查文徽領兵伐之，經年不能下。

translations.literal: When Yanxi was killed by Lian Chongyu, the generals contended for the throne; the Southern Tang seized the opportunity and ordered Cha Wenhu to lead troops to attack them — after more than a year they could not take the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Yanxi was slain by Lian Chongyu, rival generals fought over the succession. The Southern Tang took advantage and sent Cha Wenhu with an army; for more than a year he failed to capture the city.

sentences.zh: 會兩浙救兵至，文徽腹背受敵，遂大敗。

translations.literal: When the Two-Zhe relief troops arrived, Wenhu was attacked from front and rear and suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Relief forces from the Two Zhes arrived, and Wenhu, caught between two armies, was routed.

sentences.zh: 自是福州果為錢氏所有，入腹之讖始應。

translations.literal: From this time Fuzhou indeed became the possession of the Qian clan, and the prophecy of "entering the belly" was first fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Fuzhou fell indeed to the Qian clan — and the prophecy of money entering the belly came true.

sentences.zh: 蓋國之興衰，皆冥數決定矣。

translations.literal: Thus the rise and fall of states are all determined by hidden fate.
translations.idiomatic: So it seemed that a realm's rise and fall were fixed by fate beyond human sight.

sentences.zh: 徐寅，登第歸閩中，途徑大梁，因獻太祖《遊大梁賦》。

translations.literal: Xu Yin passed the civil examinations and returned to Min; on the way he passed through Daliang and presented to the Founding Emperor his "Rhapsody on Traveling in Daliang."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yin, having passed the examinations, was returning to Min when he stopped at Daliang and presented the Liang founder with his Rhapsody on Sojourning in Daliang.

sentences.zh: 時梁祖與太原武皇為讎敵，武皇眇一目，而又出自沙陀部落，寅欲曲媚梁祖，故詞及之，云：「一眼匈奴，望英威而膽落。」

translations.literal: At that time the Liang Founding Emperor and the Martial Emperor of Taiyuan were mortal enemies; the Martial Emperor was blind in one eye and moreover came from the Shatuo tribe. Yin wished to flatter the Liang Founding Emperor by indirect praise, and therefore in his words mentioned him, saying: "The one-eyed Xiongnu, gazing upon heroic might, has his courage fail."
translations.idiomatic: The Liang founder and the Martial Emperor of Taiyuan were bitter foes; Li Keyong was blind in one eye and of Shatuo origin. Seeking favor with the Liang court, Yin wrote, "The one-eyed barbarian of the north, beholding your martial glory, loses heart and nerve."

sentences.zh: 未幾，有人得其本示太原者，武皇見而大怒。

translations.literal: Before long someone obtained a copy and showed it to someone at Taiyuan; the Martial Emperor saw it and flew into a rage.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a copy reached Taiyuan. Li Keyong read it and exploded in fury.

sentences.zh: 及莊宗之滅梁也，四方諸侯以為唐室復興，奉琛為慶者相繼。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong destroyed Liang, the feudal lords of the four directions considered the Tang house restored and sent tribute to offer congratulations in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong overthrew the Liang, regional lords across the empire hailed the revival of Tang and sent one congratulatory embassy after another.

sentences.zh: 王審知在閩中，亦遣使至，遽召其使問曰：「徐寅在否？」

translations.literal: Wang Shenzhi in Min also sent an envoy; the emperor immediately summoned the envoy and asked: "Is Xu Yin there?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shenzhi sent an envoy from Min as well. Zhuangzong summoned him at once and asked, "Is Xu Yin among you?"

sentences.zh: 使不敢隱，以無恙對，莊宗因慘然曰：「汝歸語王審知，父母之讎，不可同天，徐寅指斥先帝，今聞在彼中，何以容之？」

translations.literal: The envoy dared not conceal it and replied that he was unharmed; Zhuangzong therefore said grimly: "Return and tell Wang Shenzhi: a parent's enemy cannot share the sky with you. Xu Yin reviled the late emperor; now I hear he is with you — how can you tolerate him?
translations.idiomatic: The envoy admitted that Yin was alive and well. Zhuangzong's face darkened. "Go back and tell Wang Shenzhi," he said, "the debt owed a murdered father cannot be forgotten while one lives under the same sky. Xu Yin slandered the late emperor; you still shelter him — how can that be?"

sentences.zh: 使回，具以告，審知曰：「如此則主上欲殺徐寅爾，今殺則未敢奉詔，但不可以用矣。」

translations.literal: When the envoy returned and reported everything, Shenzhi said: "In this case the sovereign wishes to kill Xu Yin; for now I dare not obey the command to kill him, but he cannot be employed.
translations.idiomatic: When the messenger reported this, Shenzhi said, "The throne clearly wants Xu's death. I dare not yet carry out the order, but neither can I keep him in office."

sentences.zh: 即日戒閽者不得引接，徐寅坐是終身止於秘書正字。

translations.literal: That same day he ordered the gatekeepers not to admit him; because of this Xu Yin ended his life holding only the post of Secretary Regular.
translations.idiomatic: That very day he barred the gates to Yin. Xu Yin never rose again beyond the humble post of Secretary Regular — and kept it for life.

sentences.zh: 江為，建州人，工於詩。

translations.literal: Jiang Wei was a man of Jianzhou, skilled at poetry.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Wei of Jianzhou was an accomplished poet.

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，福州王氏國亂，有故人任福州官屬，恐禍及，一旦亡去，將奔江南，乃間道謁為。

translations.literal: During the Qianyou reign, the Wang state in Fuzhou was in disorder; an old acquaintance served among Fuzhou officials, fearing calamity would reach him, fled one day intending to flee to the Southern Tang, and took a bypath to visit Wei.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyou era, as the Wang regime in Fuzhou collapsed, an old friend serving in its administration feared he would be swept up in the bloodshed. He fled secretly toward the Southern Tang and came by back roads to see Jiang Wei.

sentences.zh: 經數日，為且與草投江南表。

translations.literal: After several days, Wei also drafted for him a memorial petitioning to submit to the Southern Tang.
translations.idiomatic: After several days Wei also drafted a memorial pledging submission to the Southern Tang.

sentences.zh: 其人未出境，遭邊吏所擒，仍於囊中得所撰表章，於是收為與奔者，俱械而送。

translations.literal: The man had not yet crossed the border when border officers captured him, and from his bag obtained the memorial he had drafted; thereupon Wei and the fugitive were both shackled and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: Before the fugitive could cross the border, frontier guards seized him, found the memorial in his bag, and arrested both men. They were sent off in chains.

sentences.zh: 為臨刑，詞色不撓，且曰：「嵇康之將死也，顧日影而彈琴，吾今琴則不暇彈，賦一篇可矣。」

translations.literal: Facing execution, Wei showed no change in word or expression, and said: "When Ji Kang was about to die he gazed at the sun's shadow and played the zither; today I have no leisure for the zither — composing one piece would suffice."
translations.idiomatic: At the execution ground Jiang Wei's voice never faltered. "When Ji Kang faced death," he said, "he watched the sun's shadow and played his qin. I have no time for music now — but a poem, perhaps."

sentences.zh: 乃索筆為詩曰：「衙鼓侵人急，西傾日欲斜。

translations.literal: He then asked for a brush and composed a poem saying: "The yamen drums press urgently upon men; the sun in the west inclines, about to set.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a brush and wrote: "The yamen drums press hard; the western sun sinks toward night.

sentences.zh: 黃泉無旅店，今夜宿誰家？」

translations.literal: There are no inns on the road to the Yellow Springs — tonight, at whose house shall I lodge?"
translations.idiomatic: No inn waits on the road to the grave — tonight, whose roof will shelter me?"

sentences.zh: 聞者莫不傷之。

translations.literal: All who heard it were grieved without exception.
translations.idiomatic: Every witness was moved to grief.

sentences.zh: 黃滔，在閩中為王審知推官。

translations.literal: Huang Tao, serving in Min, was a judicial aide to Wang Shenzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Tao served Wang Shenzhi in Min as a judicial aide.

sentences.zh: 一旦饋之魚，時滔方與徐寅對談，遂請代為謝箋。

translations.literal: One day someone presented him fish as a gift; at that moment Tao was conversing face to face with Xu Yin, and so asked him to compose a thank-you note in his place.
translations.idiomatic: One day a gift of fish arrived while Tao was deep in conversation with Xu Yin; he asked Yin to write the thank-you note for him.

sentences.zh: 寅援筆而成，其略曰：「銜諸斷索，才從羊續懸來；

translations.literal: Yin took up the brush and completed it at once; the gist ran, "Bearing the severed cord, talent hangs down from Yang Xu's legacy;
translations.idiomatic: Yin took up the brush and wrote at once: "Bearing the severed cord, talent hangs from Yang Xu's legacy;

sentences.zh: 列在雕盤，便到馮歡食處。」

translations.literal: set out on the carved platter, and at once reaches Feng Huan's place at table."
translations.idiomatic: set on the carved platter, it reaches Feng Huan's place at table."

sentences.zh: 時人大稱之。）〉

translations.literal: People of the time greatly praised it.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The people of the time greatly praised it.)〉

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：昔唐祚橫流，異方割據，行密以高材捷足啟之於前，李昪以履霜堅冰得之於後，以偽易偽，逾六十年。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In former times the Tang mandate flowed awry and distant regions carved up territory; Xingmi with lofty talent and swift feet opened the way before, Bian with treading frost and solidifying ice obtained it after—false replacing false for more than sixty years.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: When the Tang mandate collapsed and warlords carved up the realm, Yang Xingmi with talent and speed opened the way, and Li Bian by slow, careful steps took it after him—one usurpation succeeding another for more than sixty years.

sentences.zh: 洎有周興薄伐之師，皇上示懷柔之德，而乃走梯杭而入貢，奉正朔以來庭，如是則長江之險，又何足以恃哉！

translations.literal: When Zhou arose with troops for a light punitive campaign and the Son of Heaven displayed virtue of cherishing and soothing, they then hurried by ladder-ships and Hangzhou to present tribute, observed the correct calendar and came to court—if so, then what could the Yangzi's peril be relied upon for!
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhou sent a punitive expedition and the emperor showed forbearance, the southern rulers hurried tribute by sea to Hangzhou and accepted the imperial calendar at court. In that case, what good was the Yangzi as a barrier?

sentences.zh: 審知僻據一隅，僅將數世，始則可方於吳芮，終則竊效於尉佗，與夫穴蜂井蛙，亦何相遠哉！

translations.literal: Shenzhi held a remote corner for only a few generations; at first he might be compared to Wu Rui, but in the end he secretly imitated Zhao Tuo—with the bee in its hole and the frog in its well, how far apart were they!
translations.idiomatic: Shenzhi held a remote corner for only a few generations. At first he might be compared to Wu Rui, but in the end his house imitated Zhao Tuo—no different from bees in a hole or frogs in a well.

sentences.zh: 五紀之亡，蓋其幸也。

translations.literal: The fall of the Five Dynasties was perhaps their good fortune.
translations.idiomatic: The fall of the Five Dynasties was, in a sense, their good fortune.
